newsitem.title: UK: UK wool sale sees prices up in increased demand UK.
newsitem.headline: UK wool sale sees prices up in increased demand UK.

text.p: The UK's third raw wool sale of the year opened with burst of highly competitive buying and finished with price increases for all types, the British Wool Marketing Board said on Thursday.
Most wools gained one to two pence per kg with the popular Swaledale types, used mostly for carpets, adding four to five pence to their value.
The price indicator shifted up two points to 103 since the last auction on January 15.
Just under 2 million kg was offered including almost 775,000 kg forward wools and 98 percent was sold.
Ninety-five percent of a 281,000 kg offering of next season's (1997) wool sold for an average of 106.10 pence per kg. --London Newsroom, +44 171 542 8071
